items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: we had Paul Mares, we had Martie Marcella, we had this trumpet player from New Orleans that had spent years in Vegas, Louis Prima, and Wingy Manone. Four trumpets at the same time on stage

ctx.x: Well, society has changed. Same way with baseball games. No more minor league teams.

No, everything is -- and for that reason, we have lost something. We've lost this tremendous training that these people had and they became what they are. And it's not that these people today -- I'm not faulting them, I'm faulting the conditions. And you say, in summing up, would you do it over again? Do you call where I'm living today progress, when I have to worry if my kids are going to make it when they grow up, or is the water going to be poisoned, the woods are

going to be dead? Is this better than the horse and buggy? This is what they tried to convince us about our jazz. They says, our jazz went out with buckled shoes. [now] "It's the new thing." Well, is it the new thing in life that's that great? Tell me, is it the new thing? The dog-eat-dog, like you said about the record business? They don't care about anybody, just want to make money and all that?
